claims.text: W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf and MoNbTaW are examples of refractory high-entropy alloys.
The proposed initial material is a disordered solid solution with high configurational entropy and no significant SRO.
Aging between 600°C and 900°C can induce SRO without causing long-range precipitation or phase separation in the proposed RHEAs.
Rapid quenching preserves the aging-induced SRO state.
The relevant SRO consists of non-random nearest-neighbor pair correlations with a correlation length of 1–3 atomic spacings and is distinct from long-range precipitates.
SRO formation suppresses lattice thermal conductivity in concentrated RHEAs.
SRO introduces a distinct phonon-scattering mechanism that dominates over ordering-induced phonon-bandgap effects.
SRO-induced scattering is particularly dominant when the SRO correlation length is comparable to the phonon mean free path.
SRO creates local variations in atomic mass and interatomic force constants that strongly scatter mid- to high-frequency phonons.
Potential fluctuations associated with SRO are insufficient to open a phononic bandgap that would enhance heat transport.
A mismatch between SRO periodicity and dominant phonon wavelengths increases the phonon-scattering cross-section.
The SRO sample is expected to have more than 5% lower thermal conductivity than the disordered sample.
Strong SRO suppression of lattice heat transport requires sufficiently large atomic-size and mass differences.
The hypothesis can fail when the SRO correlation length approaches long-range order.
The hypothesis can fail when electronic thermal conductivity dominates, although such domination is claimed to be unlikely in refractory metals.
The effect of SRO on the mechanical behavior of W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf RHEAs has been identified as a topic for future exploration.
Observations in MoNbTaW contradicted the prior view that dislocation glide requires breaking up local SRO at extra energy and stress.
The cited evidence does not directly quantify the effect of SRO on thermal conductivity in RHEAs.
The trade-off between disorder-driven phonon scattering and ordering-driven transport enhancement remains unresolved in the cited evidence.
Statistically equal or higher thermal conductivity in the confirmed single-phase SRO sample at both 300 K and 800 K would falsify the proposed suppression hypothesis.
